newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB Report-Rain delays sorghum, prices rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB Report-Rain delays sorghum, prices rise.

text.p: Rain in Queensland continued to delay harvesting of Australia's sorghum crop and encouraged a substantial climb in prices, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in its weekly grain market report.
Sorghum prices rose by A$5.00-A$10.00 a tonne to about A$144.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane.

This had continued to feed through to Australia's southern states, including the feed market in Victoria, but with dairy demand expected to ease in coming weeks and extra supplies of barly appearing on the market, price gains were limited, it said.

The AWB confirmed that its wheat shipments in the week ended March 7 totalled 229,037 tonnes, bringing exports so far this shipping year to 8.35 million tonnes. This is far ahead of the 5.81 million tonnes shipped at the same time last year.
On world sales highlights, AWB said only a limited range of small sales took place last week, all under the 50,000 tonne mark.
Algeria bought 75,000 tonnes of French wheat at US$174.00-$175.00 cost and freight a tonne for March, April and May shipment.
